description:
Advances: specled.package

From the specled_-vk0 test-quality gate (epic specled_-233, 2026-07-26). Both are FALSE NEGATIVES in the stale-allow-marker sweep that specled_-vk0 ADDED — limitations of new work in that PR, not inherited debt. Neither was blocking: they weaken a new supplementary check, they do not cause a false pass of the main doc-identifier lint, and the sweep does catch both rot directions on well-formed markers (proved by data-level mutations against the live ADR corpus).

Both confirmed by probe in `test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs`.

## HOLE 1 — a `>` in the reason text defeats the comment strip

`@allow_marker_comment_pattern` (:168) uses `[^>]*` to match the marker comment, so the first `>` inside the reason text terminates the match early and the marker is never stripped. Confirmed by probe with this marker:

    <!-- spec-lint:allow-code=branch_guard_fake see A > B -->

The marker is left unstripped, so the in-marker token itself counts as a token "outside the marker", and rot direction (b) — "the marker's token no longer appears on its line" — cannot fire. A stale marker whose reason contains a `>` is permanently exempt and invisible to the sweep.

## HOLE 2 — grammar asymmetry between the two marker patterns

`@allow_marker_pattern` (:167) does NOT require the `<!-- -->` wrapper, so the MAIN lint honours a bare marker of the form `spec-lint:allow-code=<token>` sitting in plain prose. But only WRAPPED markers are stripped by `@allow_marker_comment_pattern` (:168).

Net effect: a bare unwrapped marker grants a real exemption in the enforcement path while being structurally invisible to the staleness sweep — the exact "permanent unearned exemption" shape that specled_-vk0's stale-marker item was filed to close. Confirmed by probe.

## Fix

Make the two patterns share one grammar. Either require the wrapper in both (and reject bare markers in the main lint), or strip on the marker token itself rather than on the surrounding HTML comment. Then add a regression test per hole: a marker whose reason contains `>` must still be strippable, and a bare unwrapped marker must be either rejected by the main lint or visible to the sweep.

Verify each by falsification before committing — remove the fix and confirm the new test goes RED. (Epic specled_-233 lesson: run the falsifiability gate against the specific clause you strengthened, not a convenient one.)

## Also from the same review — smaller items, same file

- `:426` (the stale-marker corpus sweep) has NO corpus-size guard, unlike its siblings at `:233` (asserts `> 50` files) and `:254` (asserts `> 8` files), which exist precisely so a repo reorg or cwd change cannot silently no-op the lint. `decision_files()` has no equivalent, so an empty decision-file glob would pass silently. `:266` partly covers this by asserting `.spec/` appears, but not `.spec/decisions/` specifically.

- `:360`'s failure message says "dead in @known_codes" when the likeliest real cause is a stale `@implementation_code_files` (a new lib file emitting codes that was never added to the list). The implied action reads as "delete the entry", which is wrong. Self-correcting — deleting a real code trips the docs scan at `:243` — but the message misleads. Measured blast radius: dropping `append_only.ex`, `evidence/store.ex`, `overlap.ex`, or `spec.check.ex` from the list reports 0 differences, because their codes are all mirrored in `branch_check.ex`; only a rename-induced ENOENT catches those four.

- `:510`'s message is imprecise for a marker naming an unguarded bare code (e.g. `allow-code=detector_unavailable`): it reports "that token does not appear outside the marker on the same line" even when it plainly does, because `guarded_tokens/1` only matches the five guarded families. The verdict (remove the unnecessary marker) is right; only the stated reason is wrong. No such marker exists today.

- `:269` pins ONE live spec file by name (`.spec/specs/prose_guard.spec.md:83`) as its atom-form-severity example. Two others carry the same shape (`branch_guard.spec.md:338`, `spec_drift_trailer.spec.md:80`), so asserting any-of-`.spec/**` would survive a reword of that one scenario's `given:` clause. Failure would be loud and the path is visible in ExUnit's printed expression, so it misleads no one — it just breaks more often than necessary.

- `fixture_file/1` (:556) writes into a FIXED shared directory with a VM-local-counter filename. This is permitted for test-only paths under `specled.decision.cross_vm_temp_names`, and the filename is not fixed, so it is NOT a significant flake risk. Residual sliver: two concurrent VMs can emit the same `System.unique_integer` value, and VM B's `on_exit` `File.rm` could delete VM A's fixture between write and read. The window is microseconds and the content is identical at the single call site. Folding `SpecLedEx.TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0` into the DIRECTORY name would close it entirely.
title: Stale-allow-marker sweep has two evasion holes: '>' in reason text defeats the comment strip, and bare unwrapped markers escape the sweep entirely
